title: Chonky Cat: Demo Beta Open
author: slaughter_cats
selftext:
Chonky Cat is available to Wishlist Now on Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4047670/Chonky\_Cat](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4047670/Chonky_Cat)

I used AI for help with some of the 2D art in the game specifically at 0:40 when the buffs are shown in the video, i've also used it for help with the intro song and for help with some 3D mesh creation.

You can now join the beta for the demo if you'd like just join the discord and let me know, thanks

comments.author: Edgezg
comments.body:
OP, I have several serious questions I Would like to ask you about this.  
I've had an idea for a similar silly game using different animals.

How long did it take you to get to this point?  
How hard was the development process?  
How much has it cost you so far?  
How big is your team?

replies.author: slaughter_cats
replies.body:
How long did it take you to get to this point?  
Roughly 1 year, although i have been working on several other projects on and off  
  
How hard was the development process?  
This was particularly difficult as my main aim was to have a huge amount of enemies on screen, there's roughly 10,000 in the level so there were many months of research and development, although in my previous game i had a similar character controller (the cat) so this shortened the development for that considerably

  
How much has it cost you so far?

Probably around $2k, mostly for different assets; mostly music and some of the animals  
  
How big is your team?  
Me, Myself and I

replies.author: Edgezg
replies.body: Fascinating information. Thanks!

replies.author: YKLKTMA
replies.body: Why do you need 10,000 enemies if the player doesn't interact with them anyway?

replies.author: slaughter_cats
replies.body: The player does interact with them, not all at once but over the course of the game, they're obviously culled if not visible but yeh i have a few games in development which use massive numbers of enemies and this one of the many ideas

replies.author: YKLKTMA
replies.body:
I’d bet you don’t actually need to have that many enemies.

This isn’t a city builder, and you don’t need them to be constantly present in the scene in any form. I don’t know what exactly you spent months researching and developing, but this approach feels like a beginner-level mistake.

In practice, enemies are spawned when needed and despawned when they’re no longer needed - or, more accurately, reused through object pooling. This is all fairly straightforward to implement.

replies.author: slaughter_cats
replies.body: lol of course i don't need to but that's what i want as i already mentioned the enemies are culled when not visible so the effect on performance is negligible, i use object pooling extensively in my project but you definitely do not want to be spawning and despawning 1000s of enemies

comments.author: Fun_Mycologist_9211
comments.body:
Gonna be a jerk (a.k.a. honest critic based on my personal opinion, which is a lot of negative feedback) - 

This looks like AI slop. 

I think the bulk of the problem comes down to two things. 

First, the animations are mindlessly wonky - not in a way that adds character, but in a way that just doesn't make sense. I say this first because I think it is the most obvious "slop" indicator.

Second, there isn't much evidence of actual game design here. You have objects spawning and floating above the ground. NPCs that are spawned in an unnaturally even distribution everywhere and then all have the same basic behavior. I can see you went with the "Choose from 3", but what is there that can really materially change with your game loop? 

I hope you had fun making it. I would suggest that you focus on developing your actual design skills in a new project. AI is a long way from designing something that will actually be coherent and fun, and this reads like you got it to make something that just barely resembles a playable game. 

I think a lot of people on this sub get really excited when someone succeeds in making something that resembles a game at all, but if you want a viable product, and you're actually swimming against the appetite of most indie gamers by using AI in the first place, you need to raise the bar.

replies.body: It looks fucking sick lol. You're just jealous

replies.author: Fun_Mycologist_9211
replies.body: The bar for quality in this sub is buried in the ground.

replies.author: slaughter_cats
replies.body:
lol almost all of what you see is handmade, there's a few areas i used AI but for the most part it's hand made, the animation i'm guessing your talking about is physical animations i.e animations which also use dynamic physics, if anything that's an indicator that it's not AI lol.

It's an arcade score attack game similar to games such as hungry shark, it's not a super complex RPG it's meant to be casual and pick up and play. Again this game uses AI but only for a few small things. Early signs are this is going to do fairly well and most people like it with 5K+ wishlists prior to next fest. I'm genuinely curious to know what you've released?

replies.author: Fun_Mycologist_9211
replies.body:
Oh look, you got defensive. Glad you're optimistic about how it'll do. Certainly stranger things have happened.


But you might reconsider your response to criticism - if you respond like to any negative reviews you get, you're gonna have a bad time.

replies.author: slaughter_cats
replies.body: lol i thought as much, it's evident you don't really know what you're talking about so i'm guessing you've never actually made a real game. I've been making games for a while now so i've got a pretty good understanding of it, i think wishlists are generally a pretty good indicator of whether something is liked and will sell. I acknowledge the game won't be for everyone, no game ever is but you really shouldn't be offering advice if you've never produced anything good yourself.

replies.author: Fun_Mycologist_9211
replies.body:
I've been making games for 7 years. But you're not asking to see my games in good faith, you're asking because you're upset I think what you made is garbage. I'm not going to dox myself to appease you lol.

But that's honestly irrelevant - do you think Pollock ever asked Clement Greenberg to show him a painting, or Spielberg demanded Ebert show him a movie? lol

Your issue, aside from your game, is your inability to take criticism.

replies.author: slaughter_cats
replies.body:
honestly it doesn't bother me in the slightest if you don't like the game, you certainly wouldn't be the first lol, it's just what you said doesn't ring true of some one who knows anything about game dev, you said it looks like AI slop but if you really had any idea about game dev you would know it doesn't look like there's much AI involvement at all, except for the AI art. 

There's a ton of people who play video games, spend a few hours trying to make some games on claude or some game engine and suddenly think they know alot about making games and it definitely seems like you're one of them. Admittedly i'm not sure why i sometimes waste my time replying to people who have no idea, it's a lost cause.
